title: ESP32 OLED Drawing Pad
tagline: A real-time browser-based drawing application that turns any phone or computer into a wireless graphics tablet for an ESP32-powered OLED display.
problem: I wanted to build something that combined embedded programming and modern web development. Most OLED projects only display predefined graphics, so I built a system where any browser becomes a live drawing interface for an ESP32. The challenge was achieving responsive drawing over Wi-Fi while working within the limitations of a 128×64 monochrome OLED.

components.name: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8
components.purpose: Wi-Fi enabled microcontroller and web server

timeline.title: Web Server
timeline.desc: Hosted HTML, CSS and JavaScript directly from LittleFS.

timeline.title: Coordinate Transfer
timeline.desc: Mapped browser coordinates to OLED pixels.

timeline.title: Real-time Drawing
timeline.desc: Implemented continuous stroke rendering with line interpolation.

timeline.title: WebSocket Migration
timeline.desc: Replaced HTTP requests with persistent WebSocket communication.

timeline.title: Performance Optimization
timeline.desc: Optimized display refreshes and reduced unnecessary OLED updates.

timeline.title: Drawing Tools
timeline.desc: Added brush, eraser, adjustable brush size and canvas controls.

timeline.title: Image Upload
timeline.desc: Built an image processing pipeline with brightness, contrast, gamma correction and Floyd–Steinberg dithering.

failures: HTTP requests caused noticeable latency during drawing. Migrated the protocol to WebSockets.
OLED updates became slow when refreshing every pixel. Introduced buffered rendering.
Bitmap transfer initially produced corrupted images due to memory layout issues. Debugged by sending raw frame buffers directly.
Undo/Redo implementation was too slow using stroke replay, leading to protocol redesign.

reflections.what_worked: Separating the project into firmware and frontend layers made development much easier. Using LittleFS and WebSockets significantly improved scalability and responsiveness.
reflections.what_failed: HTTP communication and replay-based undo did not scale well for continuous drawing.
reflections.next_time: I'd implement differential frame updates, hardware-accelerated graphics, collaborative drawing and animation recording.
